neutral_title: SEBI consultation: accreditation framework for ESG Rating Providers
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought public comments on a proposal to create a regulatory framework under which entities providing ESG ratings to listed companies and securities would need to be accredited by SEBI. The paper proposed limiting eligibility for accreditation to SEBI-registered Credit Rating Agencies and Research Analysts meeting a minimum net-worth threshold, and proposed that accredited ESG Rating Providers be mandated to follow a subscriber-pay business model.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 1 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 99 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: streamlining open offer and buyback tender-offer timelines
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought public comments on proposals to shorten the procedural timelines for (a) open offers under the Takeover Regulations, 2011, from 62 working days to 42 working days, and (b) buyback tender offers under the Buy-back Regulations, 2018, from 43 working days to 36 working days, by compressing steps such as the draft letter-of-offer filing and the tendering period.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 2 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 94 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: applying insider-trading rules to mutual fund units
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on a proposal to bring dealing in mutual fund units under the SEBI (Prohibition of Insider Trading) Regulations, 2015, which at the time excluded MF units from the definition of 'securities'. The paper proposed inserting a separate chapter defining UPSI, generally available information, connected/designated persons and systematic transactions for mutual funds, along with a code of conduct, holdings-disclosure and trading-reporting requirements, and pre-clearance/contra-trade rules for designated persons of Asset Management Companies and Trustees.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 3 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 90 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: expanding the green debt securities framework to blue/coloured bonds
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on a proposed regulatory framework to (a) amplify the definition of 'green debt securities' to cover additional categories and alternative instrument types (e.g. green revenue/project/securitized bonds), (b) introduce the concept of 'blue bonds' for ocean/water-related projects and asked whether 'coloured bonds' more broadly (including 'yellow bonds' for solar) would help channel funding to green projects, and (c) reduce compliance costs for issuers of green debt securities without creating incentives for greenwashing.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 4 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 87 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering). Listing index 86 (an 'Extension of timeline' notice for this same consultation, Aug 26 2022) was the systematically-sampled item but was replaced per the outcome-independent-skip rule (procedural notice, not a policy proposal); it is instead used here as evidence E02, a legitimate Tier B precursor.

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: quantitative materiality threshold and faster timeline for corporate disclosures
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposals to streamline Regulation 30 of the LODR Regulations governing disclosure of material events by listed entities: introducing a quantitative materiality threshold (lower of 2% of turnover, 2% of net worth, or 5% of three-year average profit/loss after tax) for certain events, and reducing the disclosure timeline for events emanating from within the listed entity from twenty-four hours to twelve hours from occurrence.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 5 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 82 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: online dispute resolution for investor grievances against market intermediaries
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposals to strengthen investor grievance redressal by (1) making the existing Market-Infrastructure-Institution-administered mediation/conciliation and arbitration mechanism fully online, end-to-end, with the help of online dispute resolution (ODR) institutions, and (2) extending that modified mechanism to cover grievances against all specified securities-market intermediaries, not just MII constituents. Proposed modifications included relabelling the IGRC process as mediation/conciliation, a sole mediator/conciliator/arbitrator regardless of dispute size, and removing appellate arbitration.

notes: Sample rank 6 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 78 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: alternative eligibility route and self-sponsored structure for mutual fund sponsors
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposals to review the eligibility criteria for sponsors of a mutual fund under Regulation 7 of the MF Regulations. The paper proposed (a) an 'alternate eligibility route' allowing entities without the existing five-year profitability track record -- including Private Equity funds meeting specified experience and net-worth conditions -- to sponsor a mutual fund, subject to higher net-worth requirements for the sponsor and the AMC, and (b) a 'Self-Sponsored AMC' concept under which a mature AMC meeting track-record and net-worth conditions could continue operating without a distinct sponsor, letting the original sponsor exit.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 7 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 74 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: mandatory direct plan and trail-based distribution commission for AIFs
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on two proposals for Alternative Investment Funds: (1) mandating that AIF schemes offer a 'direct plan' entailing no distribution/placement fee, with investors approaching via a fee-charging intermediary (e.g. an Investment Adviser or Portfolio Manager) required to be onboarded only via that direct plan; and (2) moving distribution/placement commissions to a trail basis -- fully trail-based for Category III AIFs, and trail-based with up to one-third payable upfront in year one for Category I and II AIFs.

notes: Sample rank 8 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 70 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: investor consent for AIF transactions with associates
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on a proposal, developed with the Alternative Investment Policy Advisory Committee, to mandate that an AIF not buy or sell investments from or to (a) its associates, or (b) schemes of AIFs managed or sponsored by its Manager, Sponsor or their associates, except with the approval of 75% of investors by value of their investment in the AIF.

notes: Sample rank 9 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 66 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: GID/KID disclosure documents and mandatory listing for debt securities issuers
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on a proposal to introduce a 'General Information Document' (GID, valid one year) and a shorter 'Key Information Document' (KID) for subsequent issuances, to reduce the repetitive placement memoranda that issuers of non-convertible securities filed multiple times a year, and to align private-placement disclosures with public-issue disclosures. It also proposed that issuers with already-listed debt securities be required to list all future debt issuances too, plus other reforms under the NCS Regulations, 2021.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 10 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 62 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering). PDF text extraction for this document drops some doubled letters (e.g. 'Isue' for 'Issue', 'propoal' for 'proposal') -- an artifact of the source PDF's font encoding, not a content error; quoted excerpt is given exactly as extracted.

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: ICDR amendments on underwriting disclosure and bonus-issue preconditions
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposed amendments to the ICDR Regulations, 2018 covering: disclosure of underwriting arrangements for public issues (IPO/FPO); a precondition that a listed entity may announce a bonus issue only after obtaining stock-exchange approval for listing/trading of all its pre-bonus securities, and that bonus issues be made only in dematerialised form; including pension funds sponsored by lead-manager associates in the Anchor Investor category; and additional offer-document disclosure/access requirements (online inspection of material contracts/documents, complete industry report, hosting draft/final offer documents on the issuer's website).

notes: Sample rank 11 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 58 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: perpetual minimum unit holding requirement for REIT/InvIT sponsors
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on a proposal to require a sponsor of a REIT or InvIT to hold a minimum percentage of total unit capital on a perpetual (not merely three-year) basis, on a declining scale over time -- 15% up to 3 years, 5% for years 3-5, 3% for years 5-10, 2% for years 10-20, and 1% after 20 years -- with the mandatorily-held units unencumbered, and to review the norms under which a sponsor may declassify.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 12 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 56 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering). Listing index 54 (an 'Extension of timeline' notice for this same consultation, Mar 09 2023) was the systematically-sampled item but was replaced per the outcome-independent-skip rule (procedural notice, not a policy proposal); index 55 (an extension notice for a DIFFERENT paper, ESG Rating Providers) was also skipped for the same reason before landing on this genuine consultation paper at index 56.

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: board nomination rights for REIT/InvIT unitholders
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposals to give unitholders of REITs and InvITs a greater say in decisions of the Investment Manager/Manager. The main option discussed was granting any unitholder holding a specified percentage (proposed at 10%) of outstanding units the right to nominate a director to the board of the Investment Manager/Manager, either individually or collectively with other unitholders crossing that threshold, along with applying Stewardship Code principles to such unitholders. An alternative 'Unitholder Council' structure with proportional voting was also discussed.
sampling_frame: SEBI Reports & Statistics > Reports > 'Reports for Public Comments' listing (sid=4/ssid=38/smid=35), date-filtered 2022-01-01..2024-03-31 = 100 records, descending date order
notes: Sample rank 13 of 25 (k=4,start=2; listing index 50 of 100, oldest-first thread numbering).

neutral_title: SEBI consultation: delegating FVCI registration to Designated Depository Participants
issue_summary_neutral: SEBI sought comments on proposals to streamline registration of Foreign Venture Capital Investors (FVCIs) by delegating the registration and post-registration due-diligence process to Designated Depository Participants (DDPs), aligning it with the existing Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI) framework; requiring the DDP and custodian for an FVCI to be the same entity; mandating that FVCIs hold their investments only in dematerialised form (with a 6-month transition for existing controlling-interest holdings); and reviewing FVCI eligibility criteria.
